summary: This excerpt from Book 14, part 108, is a fiction scene in which a teenager named Nikko is interviewed by FBI agents Martens and Jankovich about a college student, Simon Meyer, whom he suspects may be planning something. Nikko plays two recordings of Meyer, and the agents question him about his background before Martens tells him he is too young for dangerous work. Martens instructs Nikko to stay away from Meyer and says the agents will handle the investigation, which Nikko resists as the scene ends.
one_line: A teen informant named Nikko gives recordings of college student Simon Meyer to FBI agents, who tell him to stay out of it.
key_facts: Nikko played two recordings for the FBI agents, the first and then the second.
The FBI agent said, "I can see why you're concerned," after hearing the recordings.
Nikko is seventeen years old, and the agents confirmed he is a minor.
Nikko said he used to think Simon Meyer was just a typical college student who goes to demonstrations and talks a lot.
Nikko said of Meyer, "I really think he might be up to something."
Martens asked Nikko what he was studying in school and what plays he had acted in.
Martens said he wanted to recruit Nikko "when he's a little older" and told Jankovich, "Sorry Janet. I got first dibs."
Martens told Nikko, "Given your age, we can't ask you to take on a dangerous job."
Nikko offered to introduce Meyer to one of the agents' undercover people.
Martens told Nikko to stay away from Mr. Meyer and "his big mouth."
Martens said Nikko's parents "would be all over us" if the agents put him in such a situation.
Martens said, "Bottom line: It ain't gonna happen."
Martens said the agents would look into Meyer, saying, "We have people in the field. Professionals."
Nikko protested, "But he trusts me," and warned, "If we don't act now, it could be too late."
Jankovich checked her watch and stepped out briefly to make a call before returning to the room.
